config.theme: Sprint planning for a payments team at a fictional fintech
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Sprint planning for a payments team at a fictional fintech

personas.name: Priscilla
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants the bank migration done well before the deadline

personas.name: Kenta
personas.goals: Get the bank API migration started
personas.hidden_agenda: Has been reading the new API docs at night

personas.name: Dan
personas.hidden_agenda: Wants to fix the build himself

pack.title: Invoicing and payments team - sprint planning

agenda.title: Demo feedback
agenda.goal: Review what customers said at the sprint demo

agenda.title: Sprint goal
agenda.goal: Choose between payment reminders and the bank API migration

agenda.title: Capacity
agenda.goal: Fit the plan to who is around

facts.statement: Old bank API switched off on June 30

beats.summary: Who's around; Dan's build time stands
Open bugs, accessibility and the bank

turns.speaker: Priscilla
turns.text: Good morning. Let's start with the demo. Twenty-three customers came, which is the most we've had.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: They loved the new invoice templates. The question everyone asked was about reminders.

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: Reminders for late payments?

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: Automatic reminders, yes. Over a hundred customers have asked for them.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: Is that the number in the feedback tool? I thought it was lower.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: Let me check. Eighty-seven. I was counting the demo questions on top.

turns.speaker: Priscilla
turns.text: Eighty-seven is still a lot.

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: The templates took longer than we thought, so it's nice to hear they landed.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: The dark one got a round of applause. I've never seen that at a demo.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: One customer said it was the first time invoicing felt like it was designed for humans.

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: I'll take that as a compliment for the whole team, not just the designer.

turns.speaker: Priscilla
turns.text: The sprint goal. Reminders, or the bank API migration.

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: The old bank API is switched off on June thirtieth. Nothing gets paid after that if we haven't moved.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: June is three months away. Reminders are something customers want now.

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: Fifty-two thousand invoices a day go through that API.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: How long is the migration?

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: Three sprints, if nothing surprises us. Banks usually surprise us.

turns.speaker: Priscilla
turns.text: Could we start the migration now and do a small version of reminders alongside?

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: A small version would be one reminder, sent seven days after the due date. That covers most of what people asked for.

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: That's a few days of work. It doesn't threaten the migration.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: The email itself has to be friendly, though. Nobody wants a scary reminder from their accountant.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: Friendly, with a link to pay. That's the whole thing.

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: And it should stop the moment the invoice is paid. The old system kept nagging people.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: The old system did a lot of things it shouldn't have.

turns.speaker: Priscilla
turns.text: Then the sprint goal is starting the bank migration, with the simple seven-day reminder alongside it.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: I'll write the reminder story today, with the email text.

turns.speaker: Priscilla
turns.text: Capacity. Five engineers, four days of PTO between us.

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: Our average is thirty-four. So about thirty this sprint.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: The build is the hidden cost. It takes about twenty minutes every time.

turns.speaker: Priscilla
turns.text: Is there an easy fix for the build?

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: The tests run in one long line. If we split them, it would be much faster. I'd like to try.

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: Splitting them might expose the tests that depend on each other. There are a few of those.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: Then it'll find them for us. That's a good thing in the end.

turns.speaker: Priscilla
turns.text: Then try it, but keep it to two days.

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: My neighbor started keeping bees last month. The whole street is waiting to see if they swarm.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: Ours did that once. It looked like a cloud landing on the car.

turns.speaker: Priscilla
turns.text: Back to the plan. Risks.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: Twelve open bugs. None are severe, but two are in the payment screen.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: And six accessibility issues on the invoice view. A customer flagged them at the demo.

turns.speaker: Priscilla
turns.text: Should the accessibility issues be in this sprint?

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: The two worst ones, yes. The rest can wait a sprint.

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: The other risk is the bank's sandbox. Last time it was down for a week.

turns.speaker: Priscilla
turns.text: That was painful. We couldn't test anything for days.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: Their support line was useless too. It just played music.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: It might be worth asking the bank for a sandbox status page.

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: I'll email our contact at the bank and ask.

turns.speaker: Mira
turns.text: The return rate on ACH is under one percent, right? Point eight?

turns.speaker: Kenta
turns.text: Point eight. The new API reports returns faster, which should help.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: Does anyone know who owns the reminder emails if a customer complains?

turns.speaker: Priscilla
turns.text: I think that's everything. Thanks, everyone.
